title: What Is Your School's AGI Strategy?
author: Stefan Bauschard
summary: Stefan Bauschard uses Google's leadership restructuring — Demis Hassabis stepping back from CEO of Google DeepMind to become Chair and Chief Scientist of Alphabet, focusing on long-term AGI strategy — as a jumping-off point to challenge schools on their own AGI readiness. His central move is a pointed comparison: Google has reorganized its entire leadership structure around the transition to AGI, while most schools have, at best, an acceptable use policy. Bauschard insists that 'humanity,' the abstraction Pichai invokes as the stakes of AGI, is not headquartered in Silicon Valley but literally sitting in classrooms — the ninth grader in third period, the kindergartener who will graduate in 2039. The essay argues that schools need genuine strategic restructuring, not incremental policy tweaks, to prepare students for a world being reorganized around artificial general intelligence by the companies building it.
points: Uses Google's real leadership reshuffle (Hassabis moving to Chair/Chief Scientist for AGI strategy) as a provocative frame.
Argues schools are the actual site where 'humanity' entering the AGI era lives — not an abstraction in Mountain View.
Contrasts Google's structural reorganization around AGI with most schools' minimal response (an acceptable use policy).
Calls directly on school leaders to articulate a genuine AGI strategy, not just policy patchwork.
Frames the stakes in human terms: specific students in specific classrooms, across specific graduating years.
quotes: shaping the future of AGI, Sundar Pichai wrote, is 'vitally important to Alphabet and humanity.'
